text:
michael: FYI I'm seeing a recurring pattern in prod where short-chat requests (~10-50 tokens) get starved when a few tenants push long sequences (500-2k tokens). profiler shows continuous batcher forming large mixed-length mini-batches and short lanes are stuck waiting for token budget refill.
anya: ugh that explains the latency tail spikes we saw during the 03:10 incident. do you have a snippet of the profiler output?
michael: pasted below from runtime flame; note the queue times grouped by seq length bucket: 
```
# bucket 0-64 tokens: mean queue 120ms, p95 480ms
# bucket 64-256: mean 220ms, p95 850ms
# bucket 256+: mean 900ms, p95 2.2s
# but short buckets show long waits when a few 2k seqs are enqueued concurrently
```
devon: hmm looks like token budget credits are being drained by long sequences and the refill policy ramps too slowly. are we using pure fairness per-token or per-request?
michael: current is per-token credits with a shared reservoir and per-tenant lanes. It *should* bias short requests (we have slot reservation), but KV warmup and batching coalescing turns long sequences into many small RPCs that soak the kernel fast paths.
sanjay: can you share a sample trace with kernel selection? maybe the long seqs are forcing slowpath kernels that block the GPU streams.
michael: attaching short trace excerpt: 
```
[trace] request id=abc123 tenant=acme seq_len=1800 -> selected_kernel=kv+fp16-slowpath
[trace] request id=def456 tenant=beta seq_len=32 -> queued waiting for batch formation (waiting_for_credit)
[kernel] fp16-slowpath exec_ms=1200, blocks_gpu_streams=true
[kv] cache_miss=true, kv_fetch_ms=240
```
kevin: if kv_fetch_ms is high, KV miss plus slow kernel explains long occupancy. suggestion: add short-path reserve tokens per tenant to guarantee capacity for N short requests.
anya: we tried static reservation before and it helped, but reduced overall throughput under heavy short+short mix. What if we use dynamic short-path reserve that grows/shrinks with observed short-queue backlog?
devon: propose experiment: short_reserve = max(4, min(20, short_queue_p95 / 50ms)). also lower batch_formation_timeout for short-lane to 8ms. This keeps short requests from being subsumed by long seq batches.
sanjay: sounds reasonable. also consider preemptive eviction: if a short request waits >200ms and a long request is still gathering KV, preempt the long into its own batch.
kevin: we should also tweak kernel selection hints: prefer fastpath kernels for batches with avg_seq_len < 128 even if some long tails are present (split batch if long tail percentage > 10%).
michael: summary of proposed changes for the experiment:
- dynamic short_reserve formula (as devon suggested)
- short-lane batch_formation_timeout = 8ms, default = 16ms
- preempt long requests once short waiting >200ms (age-based preemption)
- kernel hint: enforce split when long-tail fraction >10%
- enable KV warmup penalty: slightly deprioritize requests with recent KV misses to avoid thundering warmups

anya: we need metrics to evaluate: short p50/p95 latency, long throughput, overall token/s, KV miss rate, GPU occupancy, tail latency faults. add tagging to traces so we can compare canary vs baseline.
kevin: I'll wire a dashboard with these panels and an A/B scope limited to two tenants (acme, beta) and a synthetic short-heavy tenant (gamma).
devon: I'll implement the scheduler change. plan: feature-flagged rollout, 2h canary at low qps, then ramp if short p95 improves and token/s drop <3%.
michael: also add a smoke test to runtimes/bench that executes mixed workload: 80% short (32 tokens) 20% long (1500 tokens) and records queue times. use the same seed for deterministic batching.
sanjay: infra-bot, can you schedule canary window tonight at 02:00 UTC for 2 hours on dedicated pool dc-west-1-small?
infra-bot: scheduled canary: start=1765435200 (02:00 UTC), duration=7200s, pool=dc-west-1-small, feature_flag=short_reserve_expt_v1. :white_check_mark:
anya: please also annotate in the changelog that this may change billing due to slightly increased small-request tail throughput. finance alerted us before about billing surprises.
kevin: noted. I'll add a cost delta panel.
michael: action items: devon implement + PR, kevin dashboards + canary, anya run offline evals vs our eval promptset, sanjay monitor gpu/kern logs. I'll watch SLO channel for any regressions.
kevin: tagging folks: @devon @sanjay @anya. anything else?
devon: I'll send a short design note after the PR with the math for short_reserve and expected steady-state behaviour.
michael: perfect. thanks team. if we see short p95 drop >30% with <3% token/s regression we can iterate on thresholds.
anya: :thumbsup:
kevin: PR link when ready pls.
infra-bot: reminder: don't forget to roll back if error rate >0.5% during canary.
